issue_context.title: Todoist recurring tasks are deleted when completed by the todo update_item service
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When a recurring Todoist task is completed by the todo update_item service call, it marks the task as completed forever instead of just completing the current instance of the task.  

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Todoist

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/todoist/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
service: todo.update_item
data:
  item: Test daily task
  status: completed
target:
  entity_id: todo.inbox
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

> @Moonj64 Thanks for filing an issue! I looked into this and was unable to reproduce the issue with a daily task. I tried both through the UI (checking a daily task as done) and using the service call like you provided in the description. In both cases the task instance is marked completed in todoist and a new recurrence is scheduled. That new recurrence for the daily task continues to appear in the todo list in the UI as well as the calendar.
> 
> It's possible that perhaps you didn't see the task re-appear before the entity updated again? I believe the interval is set to update every 1 minute from the API.
> 
> Let me know if there are more specific instructions that I might have missed in order to reproduce this issue.

That's odd.  I've been pretty consistently able to reproduce it on the latest release (core-2024.1.2).  The steps I've followed are:

1. Create a task through the Todoist UI in my inbox with the following "Test daily task every day".  The "every day" part is recognized as a recurring task.
2. From the "Developer tools" menu in HA run the service call indicated in the original post
3. The task disappears from my inbox in the Todoist UI.

I had some HA automations that were also experiencing this issue which lead to the initial investigation.  I had recently migrated these automations over from using a REST command service call to using the "todo" service call so I can't say for certain if the issue is new in the January update.

> * Create a task through the Todoist UI in my inbox with the following "Test daily task every day".  The "every day" part is recognized as a recurring task.
> 
> * From the "Developer tools" menu in HA run the service call indicated in the original post
> 
> * The task disappears from my inbox in the Todoist UI.

Thanks for adding those steps.  I ran through them a few times.  Every time I run the service call the "test task" continues to show up in the todoist UI, just with the next recurrence incremented.  e.g. if I created it today and called the service twice, it shows it's due next on Wednesday (since it's Monday in my timezone).

I do face the same problem. My recurring task is deleted from Todoist when I use this service:

```
  - service: todo.update_item
    data:
      item: Staubsaugen
      status: completed
    target:
      entity_id: todo.familie
```

I think it stopped working with the HomeAssistant update with the new to-do-list features.

Running into this issue too. When testing, it completed the task and removed the recurrence from todoist. 
```
service: todo.update_item
data:
  status: completed
  item: "TODOIST_TASKID"
target:
  entity_id: todo.recurring_tasks
```
I think my local fork wasn't synced correctly when I was originally testing.  I tried again after ensuring the fork was up to date and was able to reproduce.

My thought for a quick fix could be that we could re-lookup the task and see if there are any changes and only set the date if it as changed. The reason the API was updated was to allow clearing the due date field -- a dataclass does not have a different representation for unset vs explicitly set to `None`, so it was changed to always set the value.

I am working on recurrence, so we can get some level of support for todoist to work. It may be hard to allow detailed edits of todoist given its API isn't directly in rfc5545 terms.

Perhaps we need to be preserving the existing `Due` information including the `is_recurring` field either way? I haven't tried yet to edit a due date changing the date but keeping that field.

What do you think?

> My thought for a quick fix could be that we could re-lookup the task and see if there are any changes and only set the date if it as changed. The reason the API was updated was to allow clearing the due date field -- a dataclass does not have a different representation for unset vs explicitly set to None, so it was changed to always set the value.

That makes sense.

> I am working on recurrence, so we can get some level of support for todoist to work. It may be hard to allow detailed edits of todoist given its API isn't directly in rfc5545 terms.

That's great (working on recurrence)!  Yeah it is a bummer how the api is designed.

> Perhaps we need to be preserving the existing Due information including the is_recurring field either way? I haven't tried yet to edit a due date changing the date but keeping that field.

So I experimented with the api a bit and it is OK to send the `due_date` or `due_datetime` when updating an item, but we also need to send `due_string`, if it is set.  This is what controls recurrence with the api.  This value is stored in the `due` -> `string` key of the item in the api response, (`"every day"` in the example below).

```json
{
    "assignee_id": null,
    "assigner_id": null,
    "comment_count": 0,
    "content": "test",
    "created_at": "2024-01-18T00:35:05.344841Z",
    "creator_id": "123",
    "description": "desc",
    "due": {
        "date": "2024-01-17",
        "is_recurring": true,
        "lang": "en",
        "string": "every day"
    },
    "duration": null,
    "id": "12",
    "is_completed": false,
    "labels": [],
    "order": 9,
    "parent_id": null,
    "priority": 1,
    "project_id": "123",
    "section_id": null,
    "url": "https://todoist.com/showTask?id=123"
}
```

So if that value is set, it should also be passed in the update request, e.g.

```json
{
  "content": "test",
  "description": "desc",
  "due_date": "2024-01-19",
  "due_string": "every day"
}
```

This resolves the issue of the task losing it's recurrence data when marking it as completed. 

 I'm not sure what the right structure of additional data should be that we store, as this is very specific to this integration.  So perhaps for now I could try out your suggestion of getting the api data from the coordinator data and making sure to pass the `due_string` in the request if that key is set.

This appears to fix the bug:

```diff
diff --git a/homeassistant/components/todoist/todo.py b/homeassistant/components/todoist/todo.py
index 5067e98642..6c421bda75 100644
--- a/homeassistant/components/todoist/todo.py
+++ b/homeassistant/components/todoist/todo.py
@@ -127,6 +127,12 @@ class TodoistTodoListEntity(CoordinatorEntity[TodoistCoordinator], TodoListEntit
         """Update a To-do item."""
         uid: str = cast(str, item.uid)
         if update_data := _task_api_data(item):
+            # In order to not lose any recurrence metadata for the task, we need to
+            # ensure that we send the `due_string` param if the task has it set.
+            api_data = next((d for d in self.coordinator.data if d.id == uid), None)
+            if api_data is not None:
+                if due := api_data.due:
+                    update_data["due_string"] = due.string
             await self.coordinator.api.update_task(task_id=uid, **update_data)
         if item.status is not None:
             # Only update status if changed
```
